title: The JABSOM exam cycle
lede: The schedule your work sits inside. Read this before you plan an exam date.

blocks.text: This is the part that is genuinely JABSOM-specific. ExamSoft imposes none of it. It exists because a delivered exam on 70-odd iPads has to be proofed, previewed on the real device, printed as a fallback, and wrapped in proctor instructions before a student ever sees it.

items.detail: All questions written, ordered, categorized, and attached to the assessment. This is the handoff point. Hit it as close as you can.

Staff preview the assessment on an iPad, review it, come back to you on anything unclear, fix errors, and preview again. They print two hard copies for emergencies and in-house exam takers, and prepare the proctor PowerPoint that carries the exam information.
Posting opens the download window so students have time to pull the exam onto their iPads. Download start is usually 48 hours prior.
Students cannot open the exam until the proctor announces the password. Examplify locks the device down for the duration.
Once answer files upload, the assessment overview in the portal gives you a first read on how the class did.

blocks.title: "It is more than just clicking a button"
blocks.text: That line is from the original OME onboarding document and it has survived every revision since 2020. Preview, review, correction, re-preview, printing, and proctor prep are sequential and they need the full 7 business days. A draft that lands late compresses the proofing window, not the exam date.

blocks.title: The hard lock after posting
blocks.text: Once an assessment is posted **and at least one student has downloaded it**, you can no longer alter questions or answer keys. Content corrections have to happen before the download window opens.

items.label: Legacy Portal: Create and Preview a Practice Exam
items.note: Useful if you want to see the taker experience before the real thing.
